A1.justification: Both PDFs describe the same MiniPLM research. Their text, equations, figures, tables and complete appendices are readable and can be matched despite formatting and appendix reorganization.

before.justification: v1 reports original pre-training experiments, downstream accuracies, language-modeling losses, ablations and proxy-model results, including Tables 1–5 and Appendix C.

after.justification: v3 retains these original experiments and adds measured resource consumption and reference/student score-agreement results in Tables 8, 9 and 11.

M1.justification: Difference Sampling, reference-model training, top-K selection and student cross-entropy training remain unchanged. The proxy-model procedure in v3 Appendix E already appeared in v1 Appendix C.3; the new correlation analysis validates an existing approximation.

E1.justification: Both versions use Pile pre-training, the same nine downstream tasks and DCLM language-modeling evaluation, including data-limited and cross-family experiments. The added resource and score-agreement analyses do not introduce a distinct task, domain or benchmark.

E2.justification: The main, cross-family and proxy experiments retain their comparator sets. New resource measurements reuse Pre-Train and Vanilla KD. Figure 7 adds a 500M Pre-Train trajectory for a comparator already evaluated for that model in v1 Table 1.

E3.justification: v3 adds an equal-training-step/token resource comparison in Appendix C, distinct from the retained equal-FLOP main evaluation. Appendix D.4 introduces holdout score comparisons against a 500M student, using Pearson/Spearman correlations and selection accuracy with a stated 0.5 threshold.

E4.justification: New analyses examine reference/student score agreement across three reference sizes and profile offline versus training-time resource consumption. These provide targeted checks of the approximation and efficiency rationale. Existing ablations, proxy experiments and case-study examples are retained.

E5.justification: Neither version reports repeated-run counts, seeds, confidence intervals or significance tests. The new correlation table supplies diagnostic point estimates without introducing uncertainty estimation or a different uncertainty-reporting practice.

E6.justification: Main Tables 1–5 and proxy results are unchanged. New results include equal-token training times of 68h for Pre-Train/MiniPLM versus 139h for Vanilla KD, and 0.826 Pearson, 0.840 Spearman and 87.4% selection accuracy for the 104M reference. Appendix F adds a 6.3% noisy-instance share; Figure 7 supplies the missing 500M trajectories.

T1.justification: Appendix C adds analytical resource-complexity claims, including memory accounting under ZeRO-2/FP16 and stage-specific sampling costs. The KL formulation, Proposition 2.1 and its proof, scaling-law derivations and proxy regression objective remain unchanged.

C1.justification: The central claims about efficient, flexible pre-training distillation, downstream performance, scaling and data utilization retain their meaning and scope. The added introductory probability-access qualification repeats a limitation already stated in v1.

C2.justification: Appendix C newly identifies teacher/reference inference as the dominant offline runtime expense and discusses measured memory/runtime tradeoffs. Appendix F elaborates the explanation involving reference-model overfitting to noisy patterns. The main interpretations and closed-source teacher limitation remain.

D1.justification: Appendix B and Table 6 newly document vocabulary sizes and detailed Llama3.1/Mamba configurations for existing experiments, including learning rates. Appendix C specifies eight A100 80GB GPUs and ZeRO-2/FP16 assumptions for resource analysis. These are additional disclosures, not demonstrated changes to the original training settings.

R1.justification: v3 adds Rajbhandari et al.'s ZeRO reference and removes Gu et al.'s Data Selection via Optimal Control for Language Models. The related-work framing otherwise remains stable; switching to author-year citations is a presentation change.

P1.justification: The abstract, introduction and some explanations receive limited editing. Appendix material is reorganized into separate results, proxy and case-study sections, with expanded case commentary. Acknowledgements and a corresponding-author note are added, while the main narrative structure remains.

P2.justification: v3 adds three tables, expands configuration Table 6 and replaces Figure 7(b)'s duplicated 1.2B panel with a 500M panel. The ICLR format changes headers, typography, plot sizing and float placement, but most figures and table structures are preserved.

improvement.justification: The added cross-family configurations improve reproducibility, while resource profiling and score-agreement analysis strengthen support for existing efficiency and approximation arguments. Correcting Figure 7 also improves completeness. These are useful, limited gains: the principal results remain unchanged, and the new analyses leave some setup details unspecified and contain notation/cross-reference inconsistencies.
